atScene.en: HF acid pain that refuses to improve despite continuous flushing is not a sign your irrigation is failing — it's a sign tissue destruction is still actively in progress. Keep flushing and escalate: consider calcium gluconate/chloride per protocol or medical control rather than assuming water alone will finish the job.
atScene.zh: 氢氟酸烧伤持续冲洗后疼痛仍不缓解，不代表你的冲洗没起效——而是说明组织破坏仍在进行中。要继续冲洗并升级处置：按规程或联系医疗指导考虑使用葡萄糖酸钙/氯化钙，而不是想当然地认为单靠水就能解决问题。

atScene.en: Six red-flag signs of vascular compromise in a circumferentially burned limb that push you toward calling for an escharotomy: cyanosis, pallor, deep tissue pain, progressive paraesthesia, a progressively weakening or absent pulse, and a sensation of coldness in the limb. Any one of these on a repeat check is worth escalating, not waiting out.
atScene.zh: 环形烧伤肢体出现血管受压的六个警示征，应促使你考虑焦痂切开术：发绀、苍白、深部组织疼痛、进行性感觉异常、脉搏进行性减弱或消失，以及肢体发凉感。复查时出现其中任何一项都值得立刻升级处理，而不是继续观察等待。

atScene.en: Chemical burn irrigation has a clinical endpoint, not a stopwatch one: keep flushing until the patient's pain has substantially decreased or resolved, not just for a fixed number of minutes — though strong alkalis (oven/drain cleaner) still deserve a 1-2 hour floor regardless.
atScene.zh: 化学烧伤冲洗有一个临床终点，而不是一个固定的秒表终点：要冲到患者疼痛明显缓解或消失为止，而不是冲够某个固定分钟数就停——不过强碱性物质（烤箱/下水道清洁剂）无论如何都至少要冲 1-2 小时打底。

atScene.en: Tear gas and pepper spray at a scene can burn YOU too, not just the patient — take the same decontamination precautions for yourself that you would apply to the patient, and don't assume your own gear fully protects you from a burning sensation on exposed skin.
atScene.zh: 现场的催泪瓦斯或辣椒喷雾同样会灼伤"你自己"，不只是患者——对自己也要采取和给患者一样的洗消防护，不要以为自己的装备就能完全挡住裸露皮肤上的灼烧感。

atScene.en: Don't assume an electrical injury is always obvious. Any patient with unexplained findings and no clear mechanism deserves a moment's thought about occult electrical exposure — a downed wire in tall grass, a fault in old wiring, or a partially insulated tool can all leave a real injury with no dramatic story attached.
atScene.zh: 不要以为电击伤总是一目了然。任何有不明原因体征、又没有明确受伤机制的患者，都值得花一点时间考虑隐匿性电击暴露——草丛里的断电线、老旧线路故障、绝缘不完全的工具，都可能造成真实的损伤，却没有戏剧性的受伤经过。

atScene.en: Heat loss is a genuine emergency for a burn patient, not an afterthought: run the ambulance heater until it's uncomfortably warm for the crew, and use warmed blankets and warmed fluids as a routine part of burn care, not a nice-to-have.
atScene.zh: 热量丢失对烧伤患者来说是真实的紧急问题，不是次要考量：把救护车暖气开到让车组成员都觉得热的程度，并把加温毯子和加温液体当成烧伤处置的常规组成部分，而不是可有可无的加分项。

confusions.en: Myth: cherry-red skin is a reliable sign of CO poisoning in a live patient. Reality: it's mostly a postmortem finding — never rule out CO because the skin doesn't look cherry red.
confusions.zh: 误区：樱桃红皮肤是活着的一氧化碳中毒患者的可靠体征。事实：这几乎是死后才出现的表现——不能因为皮肤不是樱桃红就排除一氧化碳中毒。

confusions.en: Myth: a normal or high SpO2 rules out CO poisoning or significant smoke inhalation. Reality: standard pulse oximetry can't distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxygenated hemoglobin, so severe CO intoxication often shows a falsely reassuring, normal-or-better reading — never trust the number alone in this setting.
confusions.zh: 误区：SpO2 正常或偏高就能排除一氧化碳中毒或严重烟雾吸入。事实：标准脉搏血氧仪分不清碳氧血红蛋白和氧合血红蛋白，严重一氧化碳中毒的读数往往正常甚至偏高、看似让人安心——这种情况下绝不能只信这个数字。

confusions.en: Myth: a painless burn must be a minor one. Reality: it's often the opposite — full-thickness burns can hurt little or not at all because the sensory nerves themselves are destroyed, while the genuinely painful areas are usually the shallower partial-thickness zones around them.
confusions.zh: 误区：不痛的烧伤一定是轻微的。事实：往往恰恰相反——全层烧伤可能几乎不痛，因为感觉神经本身已被破坏；而真正剧痛的区域，通常是周围较浅的部分层烧伤区。

confusions.en: Myth: an acid burn is automatically worse than an alkali burn because it hurts more right away. Reality: alkali (base) burns cause LESS initial pain but often MORE extensive tissue destruction through liquefaction necrosis — the pain level is not a reliable guide to which chemical did more damage.
confusions.zh: 误区：酸烧伤因为当下更痛，所以一定比碱烧伤更重。事实：碱性烧伤起初疼痛感较轻，却常常通过液化性坏死造成"更广泛"的组织破坏——疼痛程度并不能可靠地反映哪种化学品造成了更重的损伤。

confusions.en: Myth: every burned area counts toward the TBSA percentage. Reality: standard practice counts only partial- and full-thickness areas — superficial (first-degree, sunburn-type) burns are excluded from the TBSA calculation entirely.
confusions.zh: 误区：所有烧伤区域都要计入 TBSA 百分比。事实：标准做法只计算部分层和全层烧伤区域——浅表（一度、类似晒伤）烧伤完全不计入 TBSA 估算。

confusions.en: Myth: a burned patient found in shock on your arrival is in burn shock. Reality: burn shock doesn't set in until roughly 6-8 hours post-injury, a timeline prehospital crews rarely witness — early shock in a fresh burn patient means look for ANOTHER injury (occult trauma, bleeding) as the real cause.
confusions.zh: 误区：你到场时发现烧伤患者已经休克，就是烧伤性休克。事实：烧伤性休克要到伤后约 6-8 小时才会出现，这个时间线院前团队很少真正见证——刚烧伤的患者早期出现休克，意味着要去找"另一个"真正的原因（隐匿创伤、出血）。

confusions.en: Myth: cooling a burn longer is always safer. Reality: BC caps cooling at 15-20 minutes total (including any bystander cooling and decontamination time) precisely because prolonged cooling of a large burn drives hypothermia — more cooling time is not automatically better care.
confusions.zh: 误区：烧伤降温时间越长越安全。事实：BC 把总降温时间上限设为 15-20 分钟（含旁人已完成的降温和洗消时间），正是因为大面积烧伤长时间降温会导致低体温——降温时间不是越久越好。

confusions.en: Myth: Entonox is simply 'the burn pain drug,' so reach for it on any burn patient in pain. Reality: Entonox is explicitly indicated for burn pain AND explicitly contraindicated for inhalation injury — and since serious burns and inhalation injury travel together so often, you must screen airway status every single time before offering it.
confusions.zh: 误区：Entonox 就是"烧伤止痛药"，见到疼痛的烧伤患者就可以用。事实：Entonox 既明确适用于烧伤疼痛，又明确禁用于吸入性损伤——而严重烧伤和吸入性损伤又常常同时出现，因此每一次给药前都必须先排查气道状态。

mnemonics.name: Stop, Drop, and Roll
mnemonics.en: For a patient (or yourself) with clothing on fire: STOP moving (never run — it fans the flame), DROP to the ground (never stay standing — upright increases inhaled flame and ignited hair), and ROLL to smother the fire. If they can't roll themselves, lower them down, cover with a blanket, and pat the fire out.
mnemonics.zh: 衣物着火时：STOP（停下——绝不能跑，奔跑会给火焰扇风）、DROP（趴下——绝不能站着，直立姿势更容易吸入火焰、点燃头发）、ROLL（打滚把火压灭）。若患者无法自行打滚，就把他放倒、盖上毯子、拍灭火焰。

mnemonics.name: Coagulation → Stasis → Hyperemia
mnemonics.en: The three burn zones run worst-to-least from the centre outward: coagulation (dead, no blood flow) → stasis (at-risk, may still necrose in 24-48h) → hyperemia (least hurt, recovers in 7-10 days). The zone of stasis is the one your prehospital care can still influence — good perfusion keeps it from tipping into coagulation.
mnemonics.zh: 烧伤三区从中心向外由重到轻排列：凝固坏死区（已死，无血流）→ 淤滞区（有风险，24-48 小时内仍可能坏死）→ 充血区（受累最轻，7-10 天恢复）。淤滞区正是院前处置还能影响的那一层——维持好灌注，能防止它进一步滑向凝固坏死。

mnemonics.name: CHECK (methoxyflurane cautions)
mnemonics.en: Before giving methoxyflurane, run through CHECK: Cardiac instability or respiratory depression, Hypersensitivity, Consciousness (altered LOC), Kidneys (renal impairment), adult dosages only (Kids under 18 are contraindicated).
mnemonics.zh: 使用甲氧氟烷前过一遍 CHECK：C 心脏不稳定或呼吸抑制、H 过敏史、E 意识（意识改变）、C 肾脏（肾功能受损）、K 成人剂量（18 岁以下禁用）。

mnemonics.name: Nines → Palms → Lund-Browder
mnemonics.en: Three TBSA tools in order of speed vs. precision: rule of nines (fastest, whole-body regions of ~9%), rule of palms (fast for small/scattered burns, patient's own palm ≈1%), Lund and Browder chart (slowest, most precise, age-adjusted). Reach for the tool that matches how much time you actually have.
mnemonics.zh: 三种 TBSA 估算工具按"速度 vs 精确度"排列：九分法（最快，全身分区各约 9%）、手掌法（小面积/零散烧伤快速估算，患者自己手掌≈1%）、Lund and Browder 表（最慢，最精确，按年龄调整）。用哪种工具，取决于你实际有多少时间。

selfCheck.qEn: Work the Consensus (Parkland) formula for a 70 kg adult with 30% TBSA partial/full-thickness burns: state the 24-hour total, the first-8-hour amount, and the hourly rate for that first 8 hours. Then explain how BC's own protocol would actually dose this patient if they are hypotensive.
selfCheck.qZh: 为一名 70 公斤、30% TBSA 部分层/全层烧伤的成人套用共识（Parkland）公式：算出 24 小时总量、头 8 小时用量，以及头 8 小时的每小时滴速。然后说明如果该患者出现低血压，BC 规程实际会怎么给药。
selfCheck.aEn: 24-hour total: 2-4 mL × 70 kg × 30 = 4,200-8,400 mL. First 8 hours (half the total, counted from the TIME OF INJURY): 2,100-4,200 mL, which works out to roughly 262-525 mL/h. BC override: BC does not use the Parkland calculation prehospital — if this patient is hypotensive, the PCP dose is a flat 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres, regardless of the Parkland number.
selfCheck.aZh: 24 小时总量：2-4 mL × 70 kg × 30 ＝ 4,200-8,400 mL。头 8 小时（总量的一半，从"受伤那一刻"算起）：2,100-4,200 mL，折算滴速约每小时 262-525 mL。BC 的实际做法：BC 院前并不套用 Parkland 计算——若该患者出现低血压，PCP 的实际剂量是统一给 20 mL/kg、上限 2 升，与 Parkland 算出的数字无关。

selfCheck.qEn: Compare superficial, partial-thickness, and full-thickness burns on four features: appearance/colour, blister presence, pain level, and capillary refill.
selfCheck.qZh: 从外观/颜色、是否有水疱、疼痛程度、毛细血管再充盈四个方面，对比浅表、部分层和全层烧伤。
selfCheck.aEn: Superficial: red, blanches, no blisters usually, painful (nerve endings exposed), capillary refill normal. Partial-thickness: red and blanches (superficial grade) or extends deeper (deep grade, hair follicles/glands destroyed), usually blistered/moist, extremely painful, refill present though may be sluggish. Full-thickness: white/pale/brown-leathery/charred (eschar), no blistering in the classic sense, little or NO pain in the burned area itself (nerves destroyed) though surrounding mixed-depth tissue hurts, and NO capillary refill because capillaries are destroyed.
selfCheck.aZh: 浅表：发红、按压变白、通常无水疱、疼痛（神经末梢暴露）、毛细血管再充盈正常。部分层：浅部分层发红且按压变白，深部分层则更深、毛囊和腺体被破坏；通常有水疱或潮湿、疼痛剧烈，再充盈存在但可能变慢。全层：白色/苍白/棕色皮革样/焦炭样（焦痂），通常没有典型水疱，烧伤区域本身很少或完全不痛（神经已被破坏），但周围混合深度组织会痛，且毛细血管再充盈消失（毛细血管已被破坏）。

selfCheck.qEn: Why does an alkali chemical burn tend to cause more tissue destruction than an acid burn of similar exposure, despite hurting less at first?
selfCheck.qZh: 为什么在暴露程度相似的情况下，碱性化学烧伤往往比酸性烧伤造成更多组织破坏，尽管一开始疼痛感更轻？
selfCheck.aEn: Acids cause coagulation necrosis, which tends to form a barrier (a coagulated protein layer) that can actually limit how deep the injury spreads, and they cause immediate pain that alerts the patient early. Alkalis instead cause liquefaction necrosis — breaking down protein and collagen, saponifying fat, dehydrating tissue, and thrombosing blood vessels — which does not form a protective barrier and instead keeps penetrating deeper. Combined with the initially milder pain, patients and bystanders often underestimate an alkali exposure and delay decontamination, letting the injury progress further before anyone intervenes.
selfCheck.aZh: 酸类造成凝固性坏死，往往会形成一层屏障（凝固的蛋白质层），这层屏障反而能在一定程度上限制损伤继续向深部扩散，而且酸类会立刻造成剧痛、及早提醒患者。碱性物质则造成液化性坏死——分解蛋白质和胶原、使脂肪皂化、使组织脱水、使血管血栓形成——这个过程不会形成保护性屏障，反而会持续向深部渗透。再加上起初疼痛较轻，患者和旁人常常低估碱性暴露的严重性、延误洗消，让损伤在无人干预的情况下继续进展。

selfCheck.qEn: List BC's major-burn trauma-alert criteria and the cooling protocol that applies to every burn patient regardless of license level.
selfCheck.qZh: 列出 BC 的重大烧伤创伤预警标准，以及适用于所有执照级别的降温规程。
selfCheck.aEn: Major-burn trauma-alert criteria: partial-thickness burns >20% BSA; full-thickness burns >10% BSA; facial or airway burns (with or without inhalation injury); third-degree burns involving the eyes, neck, hands, feet, or groin; burns that fully encircle a limb; and high-voltage electrical burns. Cooling protocol: initiate cooling for 15-20 minutes total, with cool (not cold) running water wherever possible — this total is inclusive of any effective cooling bystanders already provided, and must never exceed 15-20 minutes including decontamination time. Once cooling is finished, dress the wound with sterile, non-stick, dry gauze.
selfCheck.aZh: 重大烧伤创伤预警标准：部分层烧伤 >20% BSA；全层烧伤 >10% BSA；面部或气道烧伤（无论是否合并吸入性损伤）；累及眼睛、颈部、手、足或腹股沟的三度烧伤；完全环绕肢体的烧伤；以及高压电烧伤。降温规程：总降温时间做满 15-20 分钟，尽量使用凉水（不是冰水）流动冲洗——这个总时长要把旁人已经有效降温的时间算进去，且含洗消时间在内绝不能超过 15-20 分钟。降温结束后，用无菌、不粘、干燥的纱布覆盖创面。

selfCheck.qEn: Explain why pulse oximetry is unreliable in suspected CO poisoning or significant smoke inhalation, and state what you should do instead.
selfCheck.qZh: 解释为什么疑似一氧化碳中毒或严重烟雾吸入时脉搏血氧仪不可靠，并说明应该改用什么做法。
selfCheck.aEn: Standard pulse oximetry works by distinguishing oxygenated from deoxygenated hemoglobin by light absorption, but it cannot tell carboxyhemoglobin (hemoglobin bound to CO) apart from oxyhemoglobin — CO binds hemoglobin roughly 250 times more readily than oxygen, so a patient can be severely poisoned while the oximeter still reads normal or even high. The right response is to treat clinically: apply high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather to any smoke-exposed patient regardless of the SpO2 number, verbalize that the reading is unreliable, and rely on history (closed-space exposure, duration), physical findings (soot, singed nasal hair, hoarseness, headache), and — where available — a CO-specific monitor rather than trusting standard SpO2 to rule anything out.
selfCheck.aZh: 标准脉搏血氧仪是通过光吸收来区分氧合血红蛋白和脱氧血红蛋白的，但它分不出碳氧血红蛋白（与一氧化碳结合的血红蛋白）和氧合血红蛋白——一氧化碳与血红蛋白的结合力约为氧气的 250 倍，所以患者可能已经严重中毒，血氧仪却仍然显示正常甚至偏高。正确做法是按临床判断处置：任何有烟雾暴露的患者，无论 SpO2 读数如何，都给予非再吸入面罩高流量吸氧，口头说明该读数不可信，并依据病史（密闭空间暴露、时长）、体征（烟灰、燎焦鼻毛、声音嘶哑、头痛），以及有条件时使用专门的一氧化碳监测设备，而不是依赖标准 SpO2 来排除任何情况。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Cooling duration: BC's strict 15-20 minute cap vs. the textbook's open-ended 'several minutes, then keep warm'
bcAlerts.topicZh: 降温时长：BC 严格上限 15-20 分钟，对比教材"数分钟、之后保暖"的开放式说法
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook says cooling a burn properly takes 'several minutes,' not just seconds, and instructs cooling until the burning process stops and pain is relieved — with no explicit upper time limit given, only a warning to prevent the patient from becoming hypothermic afterward.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材说给烧伤充分降温需要"几分钟"，而不是几秒钟，并要求持续降温直到烧伤过程终止、疼痛缓解——没有给出明确的时间上限，只是提醒之后要防止患者低体温。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC sets a firm total of 15-20 minutes at ALL license levels, using cool (not cold) running water wherever possible. This total is INCLUSIVE of any effective cooling bystanders already provided before you arrived, and — in the electrical burns protocol specifically — must never exceed 15-20 minutes including decontamination time. Once cooling is done, stop, dry the patient, and dress with sterile, non-stick, dry gauze; do not keep cooling for the whole transport.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 在所有执照级别都设定了 15-20 分钟的硬性总时长，尽量用凉水（不是冰水）流动冲洗。这个总时长要把你到场前旁人已经有效完成的降温时间也算进去——在电烧伤规程中更明确写明，含洗消时间在内绝不能超过 15-20 分钟。降温做完后就要停止、擦干患者、用无菌不粘干纱布覆盖，不能把降温一直做到转运结束。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (2026-06-15) p.28, p.54

bcAlerts.topicEn: Fluid resuscitation dosing: the Consensus/Parkland weight-and-TBSA formula vs. BC's flat 20 mL/kg capped at 2 L
bcAlerts.topicZh: 补液剂量：共识/Parkland 按体重与 TBSA 计算的公式，对比 BC 统一 20 mL/kg、上限 2 升
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook's Consensus (Parkland) formula calculates a full 24-hour fluid target — 2 to 4 mL of lactated Ringer's × body weight in kg × percentage TBSA burned, with half given in the first 8 hours from the time of injury — and treats burns over roughly 20% TBSA as the point where resuscitation is needed.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材的共识（Parkland）公式计算的是完整 24 小时补液目标——2 至 4 mL 乳酸林格液 × 体重（kg）× 烧伤 TBSA 百分比，其中一半要在受伤后头 8 小时内给完——并把烧伤面积约超过 20% TBSA 视为需要启动液体复苏的节点。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC does not run the Parkland calculation in the field. The formal Hypovolemia protocol indication is specifically burns >20% BSA (partial and full thickness), and the Burn Management protocol's Additional PCP Intervention is simply: if hypotensive, give 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres — a flat weight-based dose with a hard volume cap, not a 24-hour titrated formula. EMR level has no IV fluid option for burns at all.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 院前并不套用 Parkland 计算。正式的低血容量规程适应证明确写的是烧伤 >20% BSA（部分层和全层）；烧伤处置规程里 PCP 的附加干预就是：若出现低血压，给 20 mL/kg，上限 2 升——这是一个有硬性总量上限的按体重固定剂量，不是 24 小时滴定式公式。EMR 级别对烧伤根本没有静脉补液这个选项。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (2026-06-15) p.28, p.54

bcAlerts.topicEn: Major-burn severity classification: the textbook's age-tiered ABA-style table vs. BC's single blunt trauma-alert list
bcAlerts.topicZh: 重度烧伤分级：教材按年龄分层的 ABA 式表格，对比 BC 单一、直白的创伤预警清单
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook grades burns into Major/Moderate/Minor using TBSA cutoffs that shift by age band (e.g., partial-thickness major at >25% TBSA for ages 10-50 but >20% for under-10 or over-50), plus a separate burn-centre TRANSFER criteria list that uses a different partial-thickness cutoff again (>10% TBSA) — two overlapping but not identical numeric systems within the same chapter.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材用随年龄分层变化的 TBSA 界值把烧伤分为重度/中度/轻度（例如部分层烧伤在 10-50 岁人群中 >25% TBSA 才算重度，但 10 岁以下或 50 岁以上则 >20% 就算重度），另外还有一份单独的"转诊烧伤中心"标准清单，其中部分层的界值又不一样（>10% TBSA）——同一章里出现了两套有重叠但并不完全一致的数字体系。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's exam answer is simpler and does not vary by age: a major-burn trauma alert is triggered by partial-thickness burns >20% BSA, full-thickness burns >10% BSA, facial or airway burns (with or without inhalation injury), third-degree burns involving the eyes/neck/hands/feet/groin, a burn that fully encircles a limb, or a high-voltage electrical burn. Use these flat cutoffs for BC scenario and written-exam answers instead of the textbook's age-adjusted tiers or the separate 10% transfer-criteria number.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的标准答案更简单，且不随年龄变化：部分层烧伤 >20% BSA、全层烧伤 >10% BSA、面部或气道烧伤（无论是否合并吸入性损伤）、累及眼/颈/手/足/腹股沟的三度烧伤、完全环绕肢体的烧伤，或高压电烧伤，任一条即触发重大烧伤创伤预警。BC 情景题或笔试作答时要用这套统一界值，而不是教材里按年龄调整的分级、或另一套 10% 的转诊标准数字。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Burn analgesia: the textbook's weight-based IV opioids vs. BC's Entonox/methoxyflurane/oral-analgesic toolkit — no opioid in this scope at all
bcAlerts.topicZh: 烧伤镇痛：教材按体重给的静脉阿片类，对比 BC 的 Entonox/甲氧氟烷/口服镇痛工具箱——这个范围内根本没有阿片类
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook recommends morphine sulphate 0.03-0.1 mg/kg or fentanyl 0.5-1 mcg/kg per dose, both repeatable as needed, as the analgesia of choice for burn pain.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材推荐硫酸吗啡每次 0.03-0.1 mg/kg，或芬太尼每次 0.5-1 mcg/kg，均可视需要重复给药，作为烧伤镇痛的首选。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Neither morphine nor fentanyl appears anywhere in BC's EMR/PCP drug formulary for this indication. BC's burn analgesia toolkit is Entonox (explicitly indicated for 'pain associated with burns,' but absolutely contraindicated with inhalation injury), methoxyflurane/Penthrox (self-administered, 3 mL per dose, repeat once after 20 minutes, maximum 6 mL total, with respiratory depression as a caution under the CHECK mnemonic), plus PCP-level oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Do not answer 'morphine' or 'fentanyl' on a BC burn-pain question.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 在这一适应证下，吗啡和芬太尼都不在 BC 的 EMR/PCP 药物目录里。BC 的烧伤镇痛工具箱是 Entonox（明确适用于"烧伤相关疼痛"，但合并吸入性损伤时绝对禁用）、甲氧氟烷/Penthrox（患者自行吸入给药，每次 3 mL，20 分钟后可重复一次，总量上限 6 mL，CHECK 助记法中把呼吸抑制列为慎用因素），以及 PCP 级别的口服对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬。BC 烧伤镇痛题绝不能答"吗啡"或"芬太尼"。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (2026-06-15) p.65, p.71

bcAlerts.topicEn: Electrical burns: the textbook's blanket 'usually major' framing vs. BC's specific high-voltage-only trauma-alert criterion
bcAlerts.topicZh: 电烧伤：教材"通常都算重度"的笼统说法，对比 BC 明确只把高压电列为创伤预警标准
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook states electrical burns are most often classified as major burns given the risk of severe internal injury, while separately noting that LOW-voltage electrical burns fall under the Moderate category in its severity table.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材指出，考虑到严重内部损伤的风险，电烧伤大多被归为重度烧伤；但在其严重度分级表中又把"低压"电烧伤单独归入中度一类。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's major-burn trauma-alert list specifically names HIGH-VOLTAGE electrical burns as a qualifying criterion — it does not list electrical burns generically, and does not carve out a separate lower tier for low-voltage exposures. When answering a BC scenario, tie the 'major burn' classification to voltage specifically (high-voltage = alert criterion) rather than treating all electrical contact as automatically major.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的重大烧伤创伤预警清单专门点名"高压电"烧伤作为触发标准——并没有笼统地把"电烧伤"整体列入，也没有为低压暴露单独划出一个较轻的等级。回答 BC 情景题时，要把"重度烧伤"这个判断具体挂钩到电压高低（高压电＝预警标准），而不是把所有电击接触都想当然地当成重度烧伤。
